rows.knowledge: how individuals and institutions shape health status, how the global movement of populations changes health and why social and psychological factors make or break public health messages

digest.definition: The study of health across the life-course in individuals, families, communities and populations, from local to global, taking in physical and mental health, well-being, illness, rehabilitation and palliative care
distinctiveFeatures: The study of health across the life-course in individuals, families, communities and populations, from local to global, taking in physical and mental health, well-being, illness, rehabilitation and palliative care
Health is treated as more than the absence of disease and has no single agreed definition; studying it is not the same as studying illness or training to care for the sick
Multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary: it draws on over 30 disciplines, from epidemiology and public health to sociology, law and ethics, and courses choose their own mix
Reflective and reflexive critical evaluation of health and how it is represented sits at its centre
An integrated, interprofessional care approach, with patients, service users and carers as partners
Research-based, with attention to research ethics and to how research informs clinical practice and its governance
Courses range from conceptual to applied and vocational, some shaped by professional standards; the aim is to make students agents of change

transferable.text: You will be able to see how the parts and levels of health systems connect, analyse complex systems and cope with uncertainty.
You will be able to weigh up possible futures, form your own vision, act with care where effects are uncertain, judge the results of actions and handle risk and change.
You will be able to reflect on the norms and values behind what people do, work through sustainability values with others and set goals when interests clash and knowledge is uncertain.
You will be able to plan and carry out new actions that move sustainable development forward, near home and further away.
You will be able to work and learn with people inside and outside your institution, respect their needs and views, handle conflict in a group and help others solve problems together.
You will be able to question accepted ideas and practices, look hard at your own values and take a position in debates about sustainable development.
You will be able to reflect on your values, actions and feelings, think about your part in your community and the wider world and keep checking and driving your own actions.
You will be able to use different problem-solving approaches on complex sustainability problems in health and work out solutions that are workable, inclusive and fair.
